name: Khronon-Anchored Screened Preferred Frame
claimed_mechanism: The theory keeps one metric and frozen mu(y), but adds an unremovable khronon A_0 that supplies the Bekenstein M5/M1=4 preferred-frame temporal direction required for the lensing escape. A lapse-weighted matter current couples to A_0 with an e^{-y} factor, so the preferred-frame response alpha is screened in high-acceleration regions, while an independent scalar K supplies a finite canonical kinetic normalization for the propagating vector A_mu. A spatially nonlocal lensing anchor built from A_mu and A_0 separates the screened preferred-frame force from the propagating-mode kinetic normalization, avoiding the P7 collision.
predicted_weak_field: In the weak-field, low-acceleration limit e^{-y} is unsuppressed, the khronon-coupled preferred-frame current is active, and chi realizes the MOND force law through the auxiliary Legendre interpolation. The vector mode A_mu propagates with a finite speed and finite kinetic coefficient set by K, so the propagating-mode normalization remains finite. In the high-acceleration limit e^{-y} suppresses the preferred-frame current, metric dynamics approach GR, and the spatially nonlocal lensing anchor remains the residual nonlocal lensing channel without rescaling G.
inequivalence_argument: This candidate is not DC-001 because it contains a field of type khronon (A_0) and a coupling with preferred_frame=true and screened_by='e^-y', and it also contains a coupling with nonlocal='spatial', so it is not a local no-preferred-frame lensing MOND. The local metric-matter coupling is structurally accompanied by an unremovable preferred-frame khronon, which is the decisive element missing from DC-001. The finite kinetic normalization is generated by an independent anchor K plus a spatially nonlocal lensing channel, not by tuning the screened preferred-frame coefficient, so this is an architectural mutation rather than a coefficient tweak of a killed architecture.
